# casualdata

> casualdata daily publishes one new interactive data visualization every day, each on its own dated page at casualdata.com/YYYY-MM-DD/ with its data frozen in the page and its sources named. casualdata has made data visualization from everyday ("casual") data since 2005; its 2007–2011 art projects are kept at casualdata.com/work/.

Made by [Mahir Yavuz](https://mahiryavuz.com/). Each day states one finding in its title; the description below it says what the chart shows. The numbers behind each day are in that day's data.js, with sources and timestamps.

## Daily visualizations (newest first)

- [A 1960 equation put the world’s population at infinity on 13 November 2026. Until the mid-1990s the world was ahead of it](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-13/) (13 November 2026): The 1960 “Doomsday” equation of von Foerster, Mora and Amiot against the world’s population, year by year from 1700 to 2026: the population ran above the equation until the mid-1990s and has been below it since. Source: von Foerster, Mora and Amiot, Science 132, 1960 (the equation); Our World in Data, Population (HYDE, Gapminder, UN WPP 2024), fetched 13 Nov 2026 UTC. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-13/data.js
- [India more than halved its child pneumonia deaths. Nigeria’s have barely moved](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-12/) (12 November 2026): Estimated deaths of children under five from pneumonia in 2015 and 2024, for the six countries that lose the most: India’s fell from about 179,000 to about 70,000, while Nigeria’s stayed near 150,000. UNICEF estimates. Source: UNICEF, CA-CODE estimates of causes of child death, 2015 and 2024, fetched 12 Nov 2026 UTC. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-12/data.js
- [No El Niño week on record was as far above normal as the last seven](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-11/) (11 November 2026): Weekly sea-surface temperature in the central Pacific (Niño 3.4), in degrees above the 1991–2020 normal: for seven weeks running, to the week of 4 November 2026, it has been above +3.0 °C, the highest week before this year in NOAA's record, which starts in 1981. Source: NOAA Climate Prediction Center, weekly OISST Niño 3.4 sea-surface temperature anomaly against the 1991–2020 normal, fetched 11 Nov 2026 UTC. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-11/data.js
- [CO₂ has been higher at every climate summit than at the one before](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-10/) (10 November 2026): Carbon dioxide in the air in the month each of the 31 UN climate summits opened, from Berlin in 1995 (360 ppm) to Antalya in 2026 (430 ppm), measured at Mauna Loa with the seasonal cycle removed: it was higher at every summit than at the one before. Source: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, Mauna Loa monthly mean CO2 with the seasonal cycle removed, fetched 10 Nov 2026; summit dates from UNFCCC via Wikipedia. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-10/data.js
- [Every forecast miss went the same way](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-09/) (9 November 2026): All 435 House seats of the 2026 midterms, placed by how forecasters rated them before the election and shaded by who won: Democrats took 21 seats rated Republican and every toss-up, and Republicans took none rated Democratic. Source: AP results and Cook Political Report ratings via NPR, 9 Nov 2026 · not final. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-09/data.js
- [99 votes may decide a seat in Congress](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-08/) (8 November 2026): The five closest races of the 2026 midterms, drawn as crowds side by side: one figure for every vote of the lead. Source: State results and AP via NYT, 9 Nov 2026 · not final. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-08/data.js
- [Voters split by issue, not by party](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-07/) (7 November 2026): Every 2026 ballot measure on a party issue, grouped by issue, against how the same state voted for president. Abortion rights ran ahead of Democrats everywhere; transgender limits ran ahead of Republicans everywhere. Source: Ballotpedia, 8 Nov 2026 · 2024: state results. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-07/data.js
- [If the country were 100 people, 51 of them stayed home](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-06/) (6 November 2026): The 2026 midterm electorate as a town of 100 people: who voted, for which party, and who stayed home. Source: UF Election Lab turnout estimate, 6 Nov 2026; AP House vote counts via NPR, 6 Nov 2026. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-06/data.js
- [Nearly every Senate race moved toward the Democrats](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-05/) (5 November 2026): Each 2026 Senate race against the same state's 2024 vote for president. 30 of 31 moved toward the Democrats. The exception was Maine. Source: ABC News vote shares, 5 Nov 3:57 pm ET · 2024: MIT Election Lab. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-05/data.js
- [Where the light goes in November](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-04/) (4 November 2026): Hours of daylight for every latitude, every day of the year. Point anywhere to read it. Source: Computed from solar geometry, sunrise to sunset at sea level.
- [In the time it took to win this year’s Route du Rhum, the first winner had sailed 28% of the way](https://casualdata.com/2026-11-03/) (3 November 2026): Tom Laperche won the 2026 Route du Rhum in 6 days 13 hours 27 minutes. A map of where each of the 13 winners since 1978 would be after that long, at their own average speed: the first, Mike Birch, 998 nautical miles out with 2,544 to go. Source: Race times: routedurhum.com and French Wikipedia, read 12 Nov 2026. Coastline: Natural Earth. Data: https://casualdata.com/2026-11-03/data.js

## Work 2007–2011

- [News Knitter](https://casualdata.com/newsknitter/) (2007): News Knitter is a data visualization project which focuses on knitted garments as an alternative medium to visualize large scale data.
- [Value Machine](https://casualdata.com/valuemachine/) (2008): Value Machine is an interactive visualisation project which focuses on ‘conversations’ happening in the blogosphere and attempts to reveal the hypothetical economic values of these conversations.
- [Newshaper](https://casualdata.com/newshaper/) (2009): Newshaper is a tabletop interactive system which deals with re-contextualization of daily news items gathered from live news feeds.
- [Social Bits](https://casualdata.com/socialbits/) (2010): Social Bits Research Group: Research on artistic output of social interactions.
- [Sense of Patterns](https://casualdata.com/senseofpatterns/) (2011): Sense of Patterns is a series of printed visualizations designed by Mahir Yavuz
- [12 Eylül 2010 Referandum Sonuçları](https://casualdata.com/extra/referandum2010/) (2010): 12 Eylül 2010 Referandum Sonuçları ve Grafikleri Üzerine | A short article about 2010 referendum results in turkey.
